title: Amplicon Library Protocol for Metabarcoding-Based Diet Analysis in Blue Tits
author: James Nicholls
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.2jdgci6
materials: The Herculase II Fusion polymerase (Agilent catalogue number 600679) was used for all PCRs, with 0.1μL of polymerase and 1μL of DNA extraction in a 10μL reaction. For the second indexing PCR 1μL of template from the pool of the two duplicate first round PCRs was used in a 10μL reaction. Final concentrations of other reagents are: Mg2+(mM) dNTPs (mM of each) each primer (µM) BSA (mg/mL) rbcL 2.5 0.2 0.2 0.5 16S 2.5 0.2 0.2 0.5 COI 2 0.2 0.2 0.5 indexing PCR 2 0.2 0.2 0.5 Thermocycler conditions were as follows: a. initial denaturation of 3 minutes at 94°C b. cycling of: 30 seconds at 94°C 30 seconds at annealing temperature 40 seconds at 72°C c. final extension of 5 minutes at 72°C d. hold at 10°C Annealing temperatures and the number of cycles were as follows for each locus-specific PCR and the second-round indexing PCR. Ta (°C) no. 1st round cycles no. 2nd round (indexing) cycles rbcL 56 25 20 16S 54 25 10 COI 51 40 10 indexing PCR 63 - - Reactions included a 40 second extension time, which is longer than would be normally required given the length of the target amplicons using the Herculase II Fusion polymerase, in order to reduce the chance of chimera formation (following the recommendation of Lenz & Becker 2008). A slow ramping rate (1°C per second) was also used to reduce chimera formation (following Stevens et al . 2013).

After the second round PCR, samples within each locus-by-sample-plate combination were cleaned up (removing salts, unincorporated primers, and any possible PCR dimer) and normalised to a constant concentration using SequalPrep Normalisation plates (ThermoFisher catalogue number A1051001). These plates have been found to provide an effective and high-throughput method for normalisation (see Harris et al . 2010). The manufacturer’s protocol was followed, using the sequential elution option with same aliquot of buffer used across four samples to facilitate pooling (i.e. same 20μL of elution buffer used to elute 4 wells). All buffer aliquots used to elute samples from a single plate were then pooled into one tube, giving one tube of eluted amplicon library for each locus-by-sample-plate combination. An estimate of the molarity of each of these locus-by-sample-plate combinations was generated via quantification using a Qubit and the estimate of average amplicon length (363bp for COI, 440bp for 16S, 362bp for rbcL). Each locus-by-sample-plate combination was diluted (or concentrated using a speedy-vac) to 10nM. Sequencing pools were constructed by taking equal volumes from 9 locus-by-sample-plate combinations (i.e. three plates of samples each for three loci). For the blue tit experiment this equated to amplicons from three loci derived from between 275 and 278 faecal samples, inclusive of multiple controls and replicates. Three such pools were produced to accommodate all 793 samples, 30 replicates and 24 controls (9 x PCR positives, 9 x PCR negatives and 6 x extraction negatives). Amplicons within each pool were sequenced on an Illumina MiSeq, using 150 bp paired-end reads.

The Herculase II Fusion polymerase (Agilent catalogue number 600679) was used for all PCRs, with 0.1μL of polymerase and 1μL of DNA extraction in a 10μL reaction. For the second indexing PCR 1μL of template from the pool of the two duplicate first round PCRs was used in a 10μL reaction. Final concentrations of other reagents are: Mg2+(mM) dNTPs (mM of each) each primer (µM) BSA (mg/mL) rbcL 2.5 0.2 0.2 0.5 16S 2.5 0.2 0.2 0.5 COI 2 0.2 0.2 0.5 indexing PCR 2 0.2 0.2 0.5 Thermocycler conditions were as follows: a. initial denaturation of 3 minutes at 94°C b. cycling of: 30 seconds at 94°C 30 seconds at annealing temperature 40 seconds at 72°C c. final extension of 5 minutes at 72°C d. hold at 10°C Annealing temperatures and the number of cycles were as follows for each locus-specific PCR and the second-round indexing PCR. Ta (°C) no. 1st round cycles no. 2nd round (indexing) cycles rbcL 56 25 20 16S 54 25 10 COI 51 40 10 indexing PCR 63 - - Reactions included a 40 second extension time, which is longer than would be normally required given the length of the target amplicons using the Herculase II Fusion polymerase, in order to reduce the chance of chimera formation (following the recommendation of Lenz & Becker 2008). A slow ramping rate (1°C per second) was also used to reduce chimera formation (following Stevens et al . 2013).

steps.title: Synthesize locus‑specific primers with Illumina tails
steps.instruction: Order forward and reverse primers for each of the three loci (COI, 16S, rbcL) that already contain the 5’ Illumina Nextera tail sequences; all primers should be synthesized by IDT using the Ultramer option with HPLC purification.

substeps.instruction: COI forward (LepF1) tail = TCGTCGGCAGCGTCAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAG + sequence ATT CAA CCA ATC ATA AAG ATA TTG G.
COI reverse (ZBJ‑ArtR2c‑deg) tail = GTCTCGTGGGCTCGGAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAG + sequence WAC TAA TCA ATT WCC AAA HCC HCC.
16S forward (16S1F‑deg) tail = TCGTCGGCAGCGTCAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAG + sequence GAC GAK AAG ACC CTA.
16S reverse (Ins16S_1R) tail = GTCTCGTGGGCTCGGAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAG + sequence TCT TAA TCC AAC ATC GAG GTC.
rbcL forward (rbcL1) tail = TCGTCGGCAGCGTCAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAG + sequence TTG GCA GCA TTY CGA GTA ACT CC.
rbcL reverse (rbcLB) tail = GTCTCGTGGGCTCGGAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAG + sequence AAC CYT CTT CAA AAA GGT C.

steps.title: Synthesize indexing primers for second PCR
steps.instruction: Order Nextera P5 and P7 adaptor primers that contain an 8‑bp index (i5 or i7) substituted into the positions shown below; indices are taken from the Nextera XT kit set.

steps.title: First‑round locus‑specific PCR (duplicate reactions)
steps.instruction: For each faecal DNA extract set up two identical PCR reactions per sample per locus in a 96‑well plate using the locus‑specific primers with tails; use the reagent concentrations, annealing temperature and number of cycles specified for that locus (see accompanying table). After amplification, pool the two duplicates and vortex to mix well.

substeps.instruction: Prepare reaction mix for the chosen locus (COI, 16S or rbcL) with the appropriate primer concentrations and buffer.
Run PCR with locus‑specific cycling conditions (annealing temperature and cycle number as per table).
After the run, combine the two duplicate wells for that sample‑locus and mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Second‑round indexing PCR
steps.instruction: Use 1 µL of the pooled first‑PCR product as template in a second PCR that adds the remaining part of the Nextera P5/P7 adapters and the 8‑bp index; perform this indexing PCR separately for each locus‑by‑sample‑plate combination. The cycling profile is identical for all three loci except for the number of cycles (locus‑specific, see table). Run the reactions in 96‑well plates that contain 94 samples, one positive control and one negative control per plate.

substeps.instruction: Prepare indexing PCR master mix containing the P5 and P7 indexed primers (unique i5/i7 pair for each plate‑locus combination).
Add 1 µL of pooled first‑PCR product to each well.
Run PCR with the locus‑specific number of cycles (other parameters identical for all loci).

steps.title: Add extraction and PCR controls
steps.instruction: Include six extraction‑negative controls (water in place of faeces) during DNA extraction and carry them through all downstream steps. For each of the nine PCR plates add one PCR‑negative (water) and one PCR‑positive control (mix of DNA from Dryocosmus israeli insect and Inga pezizifera plant, species absent from the study area).

steps.title: Agarose‑gel quality check
steps.instruction: After the second PCR, load an aliquot of the positive control, the PCR‑negative control and a small representative subset of samples onto a 2 % agarose gel. Visualize bands: if the positive control shows no band or the negative control shows any band, repeat the entire PCR (both rounds) for that plate.

steps.title: Pool indexed amplicons for sequencing
steps.instruction: Combine all indexed amplicons; up to 280 samples can be multiplexed on a single MiSeq run using 18 different i7 indices and 16 different i5 indices. Amplicons from different loci but the same original faecal sample share the same index pair.
